doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Playing 'Chicago' on Broadway and how the band rehearses
summary: Zito has played in the Chicago pit for 25 years; the band rehearses only days before opening.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, 25 years I’ve been playing it. So it’s still going. You know we closed for Covid for quite a while you know, like a year and a half. And then we went back, you know, they were trying to get New York going, there’s more people in New York now, you know, people are coming back. So it’s a good band, you know, it’s like a 13-piece band all good players, all great players you know. One of the trumpet players is the trumpet player on Saturday Night Live, Earl Gardner, great cat man. And anyway that’s what I’ve been doing.
Ronnie, at what point does the band join, start rehearsing with the show? Where is the show at when you bring the band in?
Well the band doesn’t come in, I’ll rehearse with a piano player and a conductor you know. They do it that way, which is a drag. No bass.

But I mean it’s all technical as far as start/stop/start with the cast. You know it’s mostly start/stop for the cast. You know and then they’ll add things, they’ll change things in the music sometimes. But the band doesn’t come in until — the whole band doesn’t start rehearsing until maybe five or six days before the first performance.
Yeah. So you know that’s the way that goes.
And are the guys coming in and just sight reading at that point?

No, no. Some of the guys, well actually a lot of guys are sight reading because I’m one of the only originals, me and two other people from 25 years ago. I’m one of the only ones. Just, there are three of us that are the original orchestra members. But yeah, new guys
come in and you know it’s quite a process you know, what they go through, as far as preparing everyone you know.
